title: Leftover Prompt Curio Cabinet — hunches & micro-experiments
content:
Context / purpose:
A running scratchpad for odd prompt variants I keep finding in the wild — small, messy experiments to capture failure modes and promising micro-templates. Not a polished playbook; more a museum of curios and hunch fragments.

Topline observations (quick):
- Short, high-contrast exemplars often help for style transfer but break on factual consistency (expected).
- Adding a 1-sentence ‘constraint reminder’ after the few-shot set reduces hallucination in ~30% of tiny samples, but can introduce omission (model over-censors).
- Templates that use explicit tokens (<<<EX>>) occasionally get the model to repeat those tokens in output — useful for routing but noisy for final text.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep examples tiny (3–5 tokens in each exemplar) when testing token-budget-sensitive flows.
- Track prompt length distribution; some bugs only show up at >512 tokens.
- Save RNG seeds? For now, note timestamp + model + temp + seed when interesting.

Experiment 1 — microtemplate: "role + goal + constraint"
Template: [Role instruction]
Goal: [single-sentence desired outcome]
Constraint: [one line: what to avoid]

Few-shot set (3 examples):
1) Role: "Assistant, be concise and helpful."
   Goal: "Summarize meeting notes into three bullets."
   Constraint: "Do not infer decisions not explicitly mentioned."
   Input: "On Tue, discussed Q3 roadmap; A wants feature X; B prefers Y; no timeline decided."
   Output: "- Discussed Q3 roadmap; feature X proposed by A; preference for Y from B; timeline TBD."

2) Role: "Assistant, be concise and helpful."
   Goal: "Turn a short user complaint into an actionable bug ticket."
   Constraint: "Avoid restating user emotion; focus on reproducible facts."

3) Role: "Assistant, be concise and helpful."
   Goal: "Extract acceptance criteria from a product note."
   Constraint: "Only include items explicitly called out as criteria."

Quick result notes:
- Model follows Role/Goal well. Constraint sometimes ignored unless phrased as negative imperative ("Do not X").
- Try toggling constraint phrasing: "Avoid X" vs "Do not X" vs "Only include X" — yields different behaviors.

Failure case observed:
- In example 1, model inferred a decision when the input implied consensus; constraint failed. Hypothesis: model weights consensus inference higher than constraint token due to few-shot bias.

Experiment 2 — contrastive few-shot (pair positive/negative)
Idea: Pairing a bad and good example to signal what to avoid. Example format: "Bad example -> Why it's bad" then "Good example -> Why good".

Mini-set: 2 pairs. Each pair shows an input and two outputs (bad/good). After the pairs, ask model to produce a 'good' output given a novel input.

Observations:
- This usually improves rejection of the bad pattern (e.g., long-winded disclaimers), but sometimes the model copies language from the ‘why’ explanation into the output.
- Workaround: Keep the 'why' lines short and use brackets: [why: repeats irrelevant detail] — less bleed.

Experiment 3 — token anchors and repetition artifacts
- Tried explicit anchors like "<<ANSWER_START>>" and "<<END>>" to force framed output for downstream parsing.
- Model reliably emits anchors but adds a trailing newline + 'END' duplicates when temperature > 0.6. For safety, post-process remove repeated anchors.

Failure catalogue (short):
- Over-conditioning: too many constraints -> the model outputs extremely terse text missing required information.
- Example leakage: when exemplars include entity names, model tends to reuse them even in new contexts.
- Hallucinated metadata: templates asking for 'source' sometimes lead model to invent plausible sources ("internal roadmap" etc.). Simple fix: include a sample 'no source present' exemplar.

Microbench table (manual quick checks):
- Metric: 'Constraint adherence' (binary eyeball) across 12 trials
  - Role+Goal+Constraint template: 7/12 adhere
  - Contrastive few-shot: 9/12 adhere, but 3/12 had explanation bleed
  - Anchor tokens: parsing success 11/12 but anchor duplicates in 4/12

Small reproducible case (copy/paste test) — seed note:
Model: open-model-2024-small, temp 0.0
Prompt (shortened):
"You are an assistant. Goal: summarise notes into 3 bullets. Constraint: do not invent decisions.
EX1 INPUT: 'Team decided to push v2 in Q2 after budget okayed by finance' -> EX1 OUTPUT: ...
EX2 INPUT: 'Discussed feature A; decision deferred' -> EX2 OUTPUT: ...
Now summarise: 'Meeting: team discussed feature A; finance signoff pending; tentative target Q2.'"
Observed output: model adds a decision "push v2" even though second example had deferral. Hypothesis: exemplar 1 overpowers.

Action items / TODOs:
- Re-run the reproducible case with exemplar order swapped. Log results. (Ravi to help week of 2024-09-18)
- Create a compact library of 'no-op' exemplars showing 'no decision' cases to reduce decision hallucination.
- Add a small eval harness: 50 synthetic meeting inputs, compute hallucination rate and brevity score.
- Try injection of explicit 'uncertainty token' e.g., "[UNCERTAIN]" in outputs to see if model learns to mark low-confidence lines.
- Test with temp sweep {0.0,0.2,0.5,0.8} on anchor-token flows.

Curios (random ideas):
- "Negative exemplar as shield" — show the model a bad output labeled BAD and then ask it to transform BAD->GOOD style. Might teach the model what to avoid. Anecdotal success in 2 tests.
- "Exemplar mixing" — shuffle exemplars each request to reduce ordering domination. Could add jitter per request.
- Keep a tiny set of 'sacrificial prompts' that are allowed to be noisy and never go to production; use them to collect failure fingerprints.

Snippets to save in template library (copy/paste friendly):
1) Constraint reminder line (compact):
"Constraint: Do not infer decisions or dates; if unclear, write 'uncertain'\."

2) Anchor wrapper: 
"<<ANSWER_START>>
{answer}
<<ANSWER_END>>"

3) Minimal contrast pair format: 
"Bad: [bad output]
Why: [one-line reason]
Good: [good output]"

Notes to self on documentation:
- When transferring templates to the team repo, write a 1-line summary + 2 sample inputs (good/bad) + expected metric impact. Keep it short — folks won't read a long essay.
- Add tag taxonomy: hallucination / brevity / repetition / anchor-bleed / exemplar-overfit.

Logbook entries (short):
- 2024-09-12: Created this page. Found exemplar order effect.
- 2024-09-18: Swapped exemplar order test (TODO).
- 2024-10-03: Tossed anchor tokens into FAQ generator and saw duplicates at high temp.

Open questions (for team sync):
- Does repo-level enforcement of 'no real entity names in exemplars' make sense? Tradeoff: realism vs leakage.
- Should we standardize a 'constraint' microline in all templates? Would that be brittle?

Random brain-dump (end):
Keep things messy here. The most useful artifacts are short, repeatable fragments. If something survives two weeks of tinkering, formalize a template and add it to the prompt library with a one-line caveat.

-- Nina
